dialogues.speaker: Less-Than-Legible Notes
dialogues.text: ...The final ceremony is about to start, and soon, just like me, everyone shall be reborn from embryo. This is how the very ultimate form of life is born.

dialogues.speaker: Less-Than-Legible Notes
dialogues.text: Some of the townspeople do not seem to agree [...] But their understanding is not something we can demand. Besides, on the scale of the eternal...

dialogues.speaker: Less-Than-Legible Notes
dialogues.text: ...regard every happening as something that would have happened anyway. And in a world where all possibilities happen, everything loses its meaning. Pain, sorrow, despair, envy, they all become inconsequential. Because it was all bound to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Less-Than-Legible Notes
dialogues.text: Hope, joy, laughter — these, too, will lose all color alongside. But these are all things mankind is behooved to cast aside anyway. But perhaps... love will not fade away.

dialogues.speaker: Less-Than-Legible Notes
dialogues.text: ...Oh, Aksinya. The only sin of the world you have so wrongly pursued is its "love of sameness."

dialogues.speaker: Less-Than-Legible Notes
dialogues.text: How can one make you understand... the love of the individual? That love is the one thing that must never be reduced to sameness even if you choose to abandon it in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Do you think that Doctor Moreau wrote this...?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: But when I compare this to the handwriting information I have on hand... It is clear that "Doctor Moreau" is actually...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This "final ceremony"... What if it turns everyone in town into trees or something???

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... But where is that Doctor Moreau now?
